newTitle: Autodesk AEC Collection: What's Included & Is It Worth It?
newExcerpt: What the Autodesk AEC Collection includes, who should buy it, hardware needs and a person-by-person test of whether it is worth it in India.
appendBody:
## A practical test: is the Collection worth it for you?

Reading the list of included products does not settle the question. Run this test on your own team instead.

**Step 1: list every person who opens an Autodesk product, and which products they open in a typical month.** Not which they have installed, which they actually use. Autodesk's usage reporting gives you the evidence, and it is often a surprise.

**Step 2: group them.** In most practices there are three groups:

- Cross-discipline users who work across Revit, AutoCAD and at least one of Civil 3D, Navisworks Manage or the visualisation tools
- Specialists who live in a single product
- Occasional users who open models for review

**Step 3: price each group against the right option.** Take the Collection at {{price:aec-collection}} per user per year excluding GST for the first group. Compare it with the individual subscriptions those people would otherwise need: Revit at {{price:revit}}, Civil 3D at {{price:autodesk-civil-3d}} and AutoCAD at {{price:autocad}}. Then look at your own combinations. Do the sum for people, not for the firm in aggregate.

**Step 4: decide who stays off the Collection.** The specialist in one product and the reviewer who opens a model twice a month are better served another way. See [Autodesk Flex versus named-user subscriptions](/blog/autodesk-flex-versus-named-user-subscriptions) for how occasional use is handled.

## What the Collection looks like in a real practice

Three illustrations, simplified.

**A 15-person architecture and structural practice.** Six people model in Revit daily, three of them also use AutoCAD for details and consultants' drawings, and one runs coordination in Navisworks Manage. The three cross-product users and the coordinator are strong Collection candidates. The other three modellers may need Revit alone.

**A civil and infrastructure consultancy.** Most of the team lives in Civil 3D with AutoCAD underneath. The Collection pays off for the people who also use Infraworks for concept stage or Revit for structures. For pure road and drainage designers it is more than they need, and our [Civil 3D page](/products/autodesk-civil-3d) is the better starting point.

**A contractor's BIM cell.** The team reviews models other firms author. Navisworks Manage inside the Collection is the draw, and the authoring tools are secondary. Count how many people genuinely need authoring rights before buying a Collection per head.

## What your hardware has to do

A bundle is only useful if the machines can run what it contains. The catalogue states a few requirements worth acting on:

- Windows 11 or Windows 10, 64-bit. Several of the products are Windows-only, so Mac users should check product by product.
- 32 GB of RAM is recommended across the Collection.
- A professional-class graphics card with 8 GB of video memory for visualisation work.

An under-specified workstation makes a good licence feel like a bad one. If you are buying new machines alongside the subscription, specify them for the heaviest product the user will open, not the lightest. Always confirm current requirements on Autodesk's published pages before ordering hardware.

## Collaboration: where Autodesk Docs fits

The Collection includes Autodesk Docs as a common data environment. For a firm that currently shares models through email or a mapped drive, this matters as much as the applications. A single place for current drawings and models removes the question of which version is the live one.

That does not mean adopting it overnight. Pilot it on one live project, agree folder structure and naming with your consultants, and only then standardise. The usual failure is turning it on without conventions and recreating the old chaos online.

## Rolling it out without losing a month

1. **Pilot with the cross-discipline group.** They gain most and will find the gaps.
2. **Fix templates and families before scaling.** If you are moving from 2D drafting to Revit, the template and component library work takes real time, and the Collection does not remove it.
3. **Reassign, do not re-buy.** Named-user subscriptions can be reassigned when someone leaves. Keep a register of who holds which seat.
4. **Train for coordination, not only authoring.** The money in the Collection is often in clash detection, and nobody gets that value without a routine for running it.

## Common mistakes when buying the Collection

- Buying one per head because it feels simple. The mixed estate described above is usually better.
- Comparing the Collection with one product instead of with the real combination the person uses.
- Buying for tools nobody has time to learn. Navisworks Manage and Infraworks need a person with a reason to open them.
- Ignoring hardware, then blaming the software.
- Waiting until renewal week to review usage. Do it several weeks earlier, when changing seats is still easy.

## Buying it in India

Prices on this site are annual per named user, shown excluding GST, and a written quotation fixes the figure; ask for a quotation if you would like a different term. We issue a GST invoice on every order, and can help with activation and seat assignment. The [AEC Collection product page](/products/aec-collection) lists the current offer, and the [Revit](/products/revit) and [Autodesk Civil 3D](/products/autodesk-civil-3d) pages carry the individual products. To see which seats should be Collections, [send us who uses which product](/enquiry).

faqs.question: Is the Autodesk AEC Collection worth it?
faqs.answer: It is worth it for people who genuinely use two or more of its products, especially Revit with AutoCAD, Civil 3D or Navisworks Manage. It is not worth it for single-product users or occasional reviewers. Test it person by person rather than firm-wide.

faqs.question: What are the hardware requirements for the AEC Collection?
faqs.answer: The catalogue lists 64-bit Windows 11 or Windows 10, 32 GB of RAM recommended, and a professional GPU with 8 GB of video memory for visualisation. Several products are Windows-only. Confirm current requirements on Autodesk's published pages before buying hardware.

faqs.question: Is the AEC Collection licensed per person?
faqs.answer: Yes, per named user. A subscription is assigned to one person and cannot be shared, but it can be reassigned when someone leaves. Each named user may install on multiple machines and sign in on one at a time.

faqs.question: Should every engineer in my firm get the Collection?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Cross-discipline users and BIM coordinators gain most. Specialists in one product are often better on an individual subscription, and occasional reviewers may suit Flex. Pull usage reports before deciding.

faqs.question: Does the Collection include Autodesk Docs?
faqs.answer: Yes, the catalogue lists Autodesk Docs as the common data environment in the Collection. Pilot it on one project and agree folder and naming conventions before using it firm-wide.

faqs.question: Can I buy the Collection for one year only?
faqs.answer: The site shows an annual single-user subscription. Other terms can be quoted on request; ask for a quotation.
